text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- The Social Democrats are divided about whether or not to favour the introduction of laws which would give police greater leeway to bug private homes and phone lines.
- Opposition Greens claim the government is trying to cover-up its involvement in the affair surrounding the release of the alleged murderers of three Kurdish leaders in 1989.

- The government has restructured the central bank's pension scheme, reducing prospective pension payments for employees who have joined the bank recently. The move is said to save some 12 billion schillings, which would become available to the government.
- Electronics group Elin EBG will finance the planned takeover of a Czech electro-technical group with money from its parent company VA Technologie.
- Vienna's Chamber of Economy president Walter Nettig said recent restructuring of Austrian phone tariff system will cost Vienna companies some 1.2 billion schillings in extra charges.
- Austria is making a new effort to attract small and middle-sized companies to create about 1,000 new jobs.
- Austria's trade deficit with other EU countries jumped 13.9 percent to 108 billion schillings in 1996.
- Brewer BBAG will raise its dividend to 19 schillings after pre-tax profits rose by 533 million schillings to 1.3 billion, mostly on the back of the sale of its Coca-Cola franchises.
- Electronics retailer Koeck expects a strong rise in turnover and says it plans to invest all of its earnings over the next few years.
- Czech steel meker Nova Hut is about to select its strategic partner. Austria's VA Stahl has offered more than five billion schillings.
- The City of Vienna says it will not participate in the planned capital increase of Bank Austria, thereby diluting its stake in the banking group.

- Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger expects the 1997 budget to stay on track, while preparations for the 1998/99 budget are proving to be difficult because of strong wage cost increases in the public service. Edlinger eyes a raise in consumption taxes.
- Germany's Allgemeine Kredit and its French parent Coface have acquired the majority in Austrian credit insurer Oesterreichische Kreditverischerungs AG.
- Trade union congress president Fritz Verzetnitsch says he does not see the reduction of public service sector jobs to cut costs as a success.
- Car licensing will be privatised and handed over to insurance companies. The Transport Ministry says this should reduce costs for new registrations.
